title: Square roots and cube roots
log: 2026-11-20T12:15:19Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The closest bank point covers only square numbers and square roots, while the new point also requires cube roots, which is a further idea the card does not teach, so no bank point fits as it is or with small changes.

draft.title: Square roots and cube roots
card: A square root undoes squaring. Since \(7^{2} = 49\), we write \(\sqrt{49} = 7\). It asks: which number multiplied by itself gives 49?
A cube root undoes cubing. Since \(4^{3} = 64\), we write \(\sqrt[3]{64} = 4\). It asks: which number multiplied by itself three times gives 64?
Perfect squares are 1, 4, 9, 16, 25 and so on. Perfect cubes are 1, 8, 27, 64, 125 and so on. Their roots are whole numbers.

For other numbers, find the two perfect squares either side. \(\sqrt{40}\) lies between \(\sqrt{36} = 6\) and \(\sqrt{49} = 7\), so it is between 6 and 7. Cube roots work the same way with perfect cubes.
draft.remember: A root undoes a power. For other numbers, trap the root between the roots of the nearest perfect squares or cubes.

a.why: \(5 \times 5 \times 5 = 125\), so the cube root of 125 is 5. The option 25 comes from squaring 5 instead of cubing it, but \(25^{3}\) is far larger than 125.
a.clue: Which number multiplied by itself three times gives 125?

b.q: Mia is tiling a square courtyard with an area of 70 square metres. Between which two whole numbers does the side length, \(\sqrt{70}\), lie?
b.why: \(8^{2} = 64\) and \(9^{2} = 81\), and 70 is between 64 and 81. So \(\sqrt{70}\) is between 8 and 9. Using 7 and 8 is tempting, but \(8^{2} = 64\) is still less than 70.
b.clue: Find the perfect squares just below and just above 70.
